about: Beuk's error dictionary. Every 'says' line is copied from where it comes from: EPUBCheck lines are the message text of the bundled EPUBCheck 5.2.1 message bundle (com/adobe/epubcheck/messages/MessageBundle.properties; a %1$s placeholder is shown as …), Beuk lines are the exact strings in this repo (path in sources). Store wording appears only when it was found on the store's own documentation page (URL in sources). tests/help-content.test.ts checks every EPUBCheck code and line against the bundle.

errors.title: The mimetype entry is wrong

says.text: Mimetype file entry is missing or is not the first file in the archive.
Mimetype file should only contain the string "application/epub+zip" and should not be compressed.
The mimetype file has an extra field of length …. The use of the extra field feature of the ZIP format is not permitted for the mimetype file.
Mimetype is not the first, uncompressed entry

errors.cause: An EPUB's very first entry must be a tiny file named mimetype, stored with no compression. Re-zipping an EPUB with an ordinary zip tool breaks this instantly.
steps: Don't re-zip the EPUB by hand.
Export again from Beuk — the mimetype is written first and uncompressed by construction.
Run Validate This Book; its first check confirms it.

errors.title: The package file can't be found

says.text: Required META-INF/container.xml resource could not be found.
No rootfile tag with media type "application/oebps-package+xml" was found in the container.
The OPF file "…" was not found in the EPUB.
Container points at a missing package document
META-INF/container.xml is missing

errors.cause: The signpost at the front of every EPUB (META-INF/container.xml) points to a package file (.opf) that isn't where it says. Typical of hand-assembled packages.
steps: Re-export from Beuk; the container and the package file are generated together.
If you edited the file elsewhere, check that the rootfile full-path in container.xml matches where the .opf actually is.

errors.title: A chapter isn't well-formed XML

says.text: Error while parsing file: …
Fatal Error while parsing file: …
Malformed markup

errors.cause:
One of the XHTML files inside isn't well-formed XML — an unclosed tag, a raw & that should be &, a
that isn't
. EPUB is strict where HTML is forgiving. EPUBCheck also reports markup that is well-formed but breaks the XHTML rules (an element where it isn't allowed) under RSC-005, and one unclosed tag usually produces several of those lines.
steps: Read the file name and line in the message — that names the chapter.
If the chapter was hand-edited or pasted from the web, re-import it and let Beuk's sanitizer clean it.
Export and validate again. Fix the first error first: the lines after it are often echoes of the same tag.
sources:
content/help/guides/check-your-book.md Panes (a real EPUBCheck 5.2.1 run: one removed

gave three RSC-005 errors and one RSC-016 fatal)

errors.title: A referenced file isn't in the package

says.text: Referenced resource "…" could not be found in the EPUB.
File "…" could not be found.

errors.cause: A page, image, or stylesheet links to a file that isn't in the package — usually an image that was linked from a chapter but never embedded, or a file renamed after the fact.
steps: Open the book in the Package Inspector.
Compare what the chapter references with what the package holds.
Insert images through the image library rather than pasting links.

errors.title: The manifest and the files disagree

says.text: Referenced resource "…" is not declared in the OPF manifest.
Item "…" exists in the EPUB, but is not declared in the OPF manifest.
Manifest and package contents disagree

errors.cause: A file exists in the package, but the manifest — the package's table of contents for files — doesn't list it (or the manifest lists a file that isn't there). Readers are entitled to ignore undeclared files.
steps: Re-export. Beuk builds the manifest from the same file list it ships, so the two can't disagree.
sources: tools-bin/epubcheck.jar MessageBundle.properties RSC_008 OPF_003 (RSC_009 is a different rule: 'A non-SVG image resource should not be defined with a fragment identifier.')

errors.title: The reading order (spine) is broken

says.text: Item id "…" was not found in the manifest.
The spine contains no linear resources.
Spine entries point at nothing
The spine is empty

errors.cause: The spine is the book's reading order: a list of manifest ids, one per page in order. An entry that names an id the manifest doesn't have breaks the reading order at that point; an empty spine leaves nothing to read.
steps: Re-export from Beuk; the spine is written from the same section list as the manifest.
If you edited the .opf by hand, check every itemref idref against the item ids in the manifest.

errors.title: An internal link or anchor goes nowhere

says.text: Fragment identifier is not defined.
Broken internal links or anchors

errors.cause: A link inside the book points at a file that isn't in the package, or at an #anchor that no element in that file carries — a footnote back-link to a paragraph that was renamed, for example. A reader tapping it lands nowhere.
steps: Read which file and which link the line names.
Re-export from Beuk: notes and their back-links are generated together.
In hand-edited files, make the id and the #fragment match exactly.

errors.title: A linked document is outside the reading order

says.text: Found a reference to a resource that is not a spine item.
Links to documents outside the reading order

errors.cause: EPUB 3.3 requires every content document that is reached by a hyperlink — from the navigation or from the text — to be listed in the spine. A linked page that isn't in it can't be shown in reading order.
steps: Re-export from Beuk; it places every linked document in the spine.
In hand-edited packages, add an itemref for the linked document (linear="no" keeps it out of the default reading order).

errors.title: Manifest properties don't match the content

says.text: The property "…" should be declared in the OPF file.
The property "…" should not be declared in the OPF file.
Manifest properties do not match the content

errors.cause: Each manifest item must declare what its file contains — svg, mathml, scripted, remote-resources or switch — and must not declare what it doesn't. A chapter with an inline SVG flourish but no properties="svg" is the usual case.
steps: Re-export from Beuk: these five properties are recomputed from each file's own content every time.
In a hand-edited package, add or remove the property the line names on that item.

errors.title: Duplicate files, differently-cased

says.text: Duplicate entry in the ZIP file: "…" (file names must be unique after Unicode canonical normalization and full case folding).

errors.cause: The package holds Chapter1.xhtml and chapter1.xhtml, or a manifest identifier used twice. Some systems treat those as the same name and collide.
steps: The validator's duplicate-identifier check catches the manifest version (it reports under Manifest and package contents disagree).
For filenames, re-export rather than hand-renaming files inside a package.

errors.title: Book ID marked as a UUID but invalid

says.text: "dc:identifier" value "…" is marked as a UUID, but is an invalid UUID.

errors.cause: Books saved by older Beuk builds carry an id like urn:uuid:sk3j9x2a-s8f7d6e5. Beuk replaces it with a real UUID whenever the book arrives on the desk.
steps: Open the book in the studio once — the id is repaired automatically.
Export again; the new file carries the corrected id.
sources: README.md 'Local-first saving (studio)' — Book IDs from older builds

errors.title: The navigation is incomplete

says.text: TOC attribute references resource with non-NCX mime type; "application/x-dtbncx+xml" is expected.
Navigation landmarks are incomplete
No navigation document declared
No NCX for older readers
NCX problems

errors.cause: EPUB 3 readers use the navigation document — its table of contents and landmarks (contents, the start of the body text, the cover). The NCX is the old EPUB 2 navigation file older Kindles still read. If either is missing, or the NCX's entries point at files that aren't there, readers lose their table of contents.
steps: Re-export; Beuk always generates the NCX alongside the EPUB 3 navigation, in reading order.
In a hand-edited package, check the spine's toc attribute names the NCX item.

errors.title: An image has no alt text

says.text: Images without alt text

errors.cause: Screen-reader users hear nothing where the picture is. Beuk's validator treats a missing description as an error; decorative ornaments (aria-hidden) are skipped by design.
steps: Find the image the line names in the strip under the editor.
Add one plain sentence describing what the picture shows.
Export and validate again.
sources: The bundled EPUBCheck 5.2.1 message bundle has no message for a missing img alt attribute, so no EPUBCheck code is mapped.

errors.title: Required metadata is missing

says.text: Required metadata is missing

errors.cause: The package lacks one of a title, an author, an identifier or a language. Most stores reject a book that arrives without them.
steps: Open Project Settings and fill in the field the line names.
Export and validate again.

errors.title: No ISBN — the book's own identifier is used

says.text: No ISBN — the book's UUID is the identifier

errors.cause: Without an ISBN in Project Settings the package identifies the book by its own UUID. That is valid EPUB and fine for direct sales; most store programmes want an ISBN, or assign their own ID on ingest. A warning, not a failure.
steps: Have an ISBN? Add it in Project Settings and export again.
No ISBN? You can ship as it is — Beuk never invents one.

errors.title: No book description

says.text: No book description

errors.cause: Project Settings has no description, so the package carries no dc:description. The book still opens and reads without one, but stores show the description on the book's page. A warning, not a failure.
steps: Add a description in Project Settings and export again.

errors.title: The cover is missing or not declared

says.text: No cover image
Cover image is packaged but not declared
Cover declaration is incomplete

errors.cause: With no cover uploaded the book is still valid, and the validator says so as a warning — but nearly every store requires a cover before it lists a book. A cover file that ships without properties="cover-image" (or without the legacy cover meta) is an error: stores would not treat it as the cover.
steps: Upload a cover in Project Settings.
Export again — the cover is declared, given a cover page and a cover landmark.

errors.title: Kindle says the cover is too small
errors.cause: Not an EPUB error at all — a catalogue rule. KDP's cover guidelines give the ideal size as 2,560 pixels in height by 1,600 pixels in width, and require at least 500 pixels on the longest side; KDP shows a warning at upload when a cover is smaller than recommended.
steps: Upload the largest cover you have in Project Settings.
Re-export with the KDP preset.
sources: https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G6GTK3T3NUHKLEFX (fetched 2026-10-25; the page does not quote the warning's exact words, so none are shown here)

errors.title: Apple Books refuses a large image
errors.cause: Apple's importer adds its own limits. Its Books Asset Guide (changes in 5.2.14) raised the limit for interior book images from 4 million to 5.6 million pixels — width times height, whatever the file size.
steps: Export with the Apple Books preset.
Keep individual images near 2048 px on the long side — ample for any e-reader screen.
sources: https://help.apple.com/itc/booksassetguide/en.lproj/itc618428401.html (fetched 2026-10-25; it gives no error-message text, so none is shown here)

errors.title: A server check ran out of time

says.text: EPUBCheck did not finish within 120000 ms and was stopped.
Ghostscript did not finish within 1800000 ms (PDFX_TIMEOUT_MS) and was stopped

errors.cause: Each server job step gets a fixed allowance: EPUBCheck and the print renderer 2 minutes by default (JOB_TIMEOUT_MS), the PDF/X conversion 30 minutes for every part of the book together (PDFX_TIMEOUT_MS; a long book is converted 40 pages at a time and the message names the pages it was on). Pages with any transparency are flattened to images, which is slow on picture-heavy books. An overrun is stopped and the job is reported as failed, not left hanging. The numbers in the message are this server's settings.
steps: Run the check again — a busy moment is the usual cause.
If it fails the same way twice, the book may need longer than this server allows; the job id identifies the run.
sources: src/jobs/tools.ts runEpubCheck and runPdfx timeout messages

errors.title: Too many server jobs waiting

says.text: you already have 2 jobs waiting or running (the limit is 2); start this one when one of them finishes
the server job queue is full right now; please try again in a few minutes

errors.cause: One account can hold two server jobs (EPUBCheck or PDF/X) queued or running at a time, and the whole server twenty, so one book cannot crowd out everyone else. Both limits are server settings (JOB_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER, JOB_MAX_QUEUED); the message names this server's numbers. No job is created when the answer is 429 or 503.
steps: Wait for a running job to finish.
Then start the next one.

errors.title: Two devices saved different copies

says.text: This book changed in two places
revision conflict: the shelf copy has changed

errors.cause: You edited the same book in two places. Beuk never overwrites silently — it asks which copy wins.
steps: Choose Keep mine, Use the shelf copy, or Keep both.
Not sure? Keep both — the shelf copy is kept as a snapshot in History, word for word.

errors.title: This browser is blocking storage

says.text: Not saved — this browser is blocking storage
Not saved — this device's storage is full

errors.cause: Private windows and some privacy settings stop the studio from saving on this device, and a full disk does the same. Your writing is still on screen, but it isn't kept.
steps: Export a backup now (the header indicator offers it).
Open Beuk in a normal window, or allow site storage, or free some space.
Sign in so the shelf keeps a copy too.

errors.title: This share link is closed

says.text: This reading copy is closed
The writer has closed this reading copy.
The reading period for this copy has ended.
this reading copy is closed

errors.cause: The writer revoked this reading link, or its expiry date passed. Nothing is wrong on the reader's side. Comments left before then stay with the writer, on the writer's side of the link.
steps: Ask the writer for a fresh link.
No account is needed to read or comment.
